questions.text: What are the top module name and file name, and which module exposes the h_* register port for the bench to drive directly (the top-level interface lists no h_* ports and no rst port)? Is jtag_bus instantiated inside the top, and what are the instance and port names?
questions.topic: Names, files and the build target
questions.answer: The top-level module is `p1_clkmeter_top` in `rtl/p1_clkmeter_top.sv`. The module that exposes the h_* register port is the separate core `p1_clkmeter_core` in `rtl/p1_clkmeter_core.sv`, with ports `clk`, `rst` (active high), `h_we`, `h_re`, `h_addr[11:0]`, `h_wdata[31:0]`, `h_rdata[31:0]` and the design's own signals. The bench drives the core directly. The specification does not settle the rest. It does not say where `jtag_bus` is instantiated, or what its instance name or port names are. It says only that the register bus module in `data/jtag_bus.sv` is used unchanged and gives the design a register port in the clock domain of the `clk` you give it. It also does not describe the top-level port list.
questions.evidence: Names and files: the top-level module is named `p1_clkmeter_top` in `rtl/p1_clkmeter_top.sv`; the register-port core (the logic behind the `h_*` port, with no vendor primitive) is a separate module named `p1_clkmeter_core` in `rtl/p1_clkmeter_core.sv`, with ports `clk`, `rst` (active high), `h_we`, `h_re`, `h_addr[11:0]`, `h_wdata[31:0]`, `h_rdata[31:0]` and the design's own signals. Files are SystemVerilog (`.sv`). The bench drives the core.

questions.answer: Settled by the spec: the top-level module is `p1_clkmeter_top` in `rtl/p1_clkmeter_top.sv`. questions.text: What GATE_ACTUAL does that completed measurement report: the old value 156250000, or the new value 2000000? (Scenario: A measurement is running with GATE_LEN=156250000 (BUSY=1). The host writes GATE_LEN=2000000 on the same clock in which BUSY falls and DONE sets.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: The old value, 156250000. GATE_ACTUAL is the number of reference cycles in the gate that just completed, and that gate ran for 156250000 cycles. COUNT and GATE_ACTUAL hold their final results in the same clock in which DONE is set, so a GATE_LEN write on that clock cannot change them. The specification does not say whether that late write is accepted or ignored, but either way the completed measurement reports 156250000.
questions.evidence: DONE is set when the last reference cycle of the gate has been counted and COUNT and GATE_ACTUAL hold the final results in the same clock; DONE stays set until the next accepted START.

questions.text: After reset, what does SCRATCH read as (decimal), and what is the GATE_LEN value reported at the next START? (Scenario: SCRATCH was written 0xDEADBEEF and GATE_LEN written 5000, LED_EN set to 1, then reset occurs.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: SCRATCH reads 0 after reset. GATE_LEN returns to its default of 156,250,000 (one second), so the next START uses that gate length and not the 5000 written before reset. LED_EN is also 0 after reset, so both LEDs are off.
questions.evidence: - Reset: every register resets to 0 except GATE_LEN (156,250,000) and ID. STATUS.BUSY and STATUS.DONE are 0 after reset. COUNT, GATE_ACTUAL and MEAS_DONE are 0 after reset. LED_EN is 0 after reset, both LEDs are off.

questions.text: Is the START accepted and a new measurement begun? (Scenario: h_we writes CTRL with START=1 on the very clock in which a previous measurement's BUSY clears (BUSY is seen 1 by the host but falls in that clock).) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?

Is GATE_ACTUAL 4294967295 after completion? (Scenario: GATE_LEN is written 0xFFFFFFFF (about 27.5 s gate), measurement started and allowed to complete.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. GATE_ACTUAL must equal the gate length that was set, so with GATE_LEN = 0xFFFFFFFF it reads 4294967295 after completion. The specification clamps GATE_LEN only below 1,000 and sets no upper limit.
questions.evidence: - When it is done I read how many C3 edges were counted, and how many reference cycles the gate actually lasted (it must equal the gate length I asked for).

questions.text: On re-enable, does led[0] start from 0 with its toggle count restarted at 12500000 cycles? (Scenario: LED_EN is written 1 after reset, then 0, then 1 again after led[0]=1 had been shown.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?

After release, are BUSY=0, DONE=0, MEAS_DONE=0 and both LEDs=0 all true? (Scenario: During a measurement with BUSY=1 and LED_EN=1, the internal rst is asserted for 8 clocks and then released.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. After reset, BUSY=0, DONE=0, MEAS_DONE=0, and LED_EN=0 with both LEDs off. The spec states these reset values without conditions, so they apply when reset hits during a measurement. GATE_LEN returns to 156,250,000, and COUNT and GATE_ACTUAL return to 0.
questions.evidence: - Reset: every register resets to 0 except GATE_LEN (156,250,000) and ID. STATUS.BUSY and STATUS.DONE are 0 after reset. COUNT, GATE_ACTUAL and MEAS_DONE are 0 after reset. LED_EN is 0 after reset, both LEDs are off.

questions.text: Do both LEDs go to 0 and does the measurement start? (Scenario: A single CTRL write sets LED_EN=0 and START=1 while BUSY=0, with LED counters mid-count and led[0]=1.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes to both. With LED_EN=0 both LEDs read 0, so led[0] goes to 0. START is accepted because BUSY=0, so the measurement runs. The spec does not say what the LED counters do when LED_EN is turned off, and the question does not ask about that.
questions.evidence: - LED 0 toggles every 12,500,000 cycles of the C3 clock and LED 1 every 78,125,000 cycles of the reference clock, only while LED_EN is 1; with LED_EN 0 both are 0.
